negotiation.legacySelection: For any pre-existing intake operation, absence of the header or the exact locked v7 ID selects the complete locked v7 request, response and behavior. This includes pre-existing six-sheet SOP and its media operation, not only FAQ. Return all otherwise eligible FAQ and preserve v7 authorization, limits, paging and errors; old snapshot SOP arrays remain empty as required by v7.
negotiation.successorSelection: The exact complete ID from the deployed successor manifest selects the successor view; a prefix, profile, proposed number or merely pattern-matching ID is insufficient. Every new graph operation, graph candidate, graph media binding and graph projection requires this exact ID. The published ID does not exist until a real source commit and reviewed export.
negotiation.unsupported: After normal authentication and resource authorization, an empty, duplicated, malformed or unsupported header, or a legacy selection requesting an exclusively new graph resource or operation, must fail before writes or protected disclosure. Use HTTP 409 with the original v7 IntakeError shape and reason UPGRADE_REQUIRED where negotiation has not selected the successor, including legacy access to an exclusively new graph resource. Do not emit a v9-only error reason to a v7 client. A normal, representable old request is never rejected solely because graph content also exists.
negotiation.consistency: Keep the selected view on all pages, operations, receipts, errors and media reads. Bind or revalidate the view for cursor and operation retries; reject a mixed-view continuation before protected disclosure without creating duplicate writes. Apply original authorization and no-disclosure behavior in either view.
negotiation.fullRelease: The separate /v1/announce/snapshot operation and its reachable schemas retain the locked v7 contract. Preserve the complete eligible four-domain FAQ release, its existing source and lease semantics, and its current pointer. The SOP graph uses the existing release lineage and the negotiated intake graph projection; the v7 intake snapshot keeps its required empty SOP arrays. No parallel publication or catalog is introduced.

laterUserDecisions.source: User decisions in this conversation after the earlier graph implementation approval; wording is a summary, not a new approval record.
decisions: An active flow may continue its original published version after temporary loss and restoration of current authorization, while the original content remains valid and all current dependencies are rechecked.
When the login session expires automatically, the same account may log in again and resume the same eligible active flow after reauthorization and rebinding.
An explicit logout or normal application close ends the active flow. The server cannot promise to detect every abnormal exit without a separate heartbeat or recovery mechanism.
Publishing a new version does not interrupt an already active valid flow; a newly opened flow uses the current published version. Revocation or actual content invalidation stops protected actions.
